## Setup

[The original challenge](https://adventofcode.com/2025/day/1)

## My thoughts

We did this as part of our Coffee & Code in The Strategy Unit. I paired up with a non-coding analysts.
Some of the groups did part 1 in Excel. We wrote a simple for loop in R. We didn't get time to do part 2.

Modulo arithmetic often features heavily in these puzzles. And it's interesting because although you probably never studied it under undergrad mathematics - almost everyone learnt to do "clock arithmetic" in primary school.

When chatting with the analyst about the approach we talked about 

- the importance of readable variable names
- how to build up code by starting with a small section you can follow `lines <- lines[1:5]`
- how renaming variables can cause bugs (and the important of cleaning your environment)
- more bug spotting (we originally accidentally left a variable called `starting_position` in the if statement which broke the loop)

## Part 1

```{r}
lines <- readLines("input.txt")

results <- vector(length = length(lines))
position <- 50

for (counter in 1:length(lines)) {
instruction <- lines[counter]
  
direction <- substr(instruction, 1, 1)
amount <- as.numeric(substr(instruction, 2, nchar(instruction)))

if (direction == "R") {
  position = (position + amount) %% 100
} else if (direction == "L") {
  position = (position - amount) %% 100
}

results[counter] <- position    
}

sum(results == 0)
```
